key_insight: In agentic reinforcement learning, using a privileged self-teacher is not always beneficial: the teacher can be unreliable, and its help matters more at some stages than others. RetireOPD introduces a self-retiring distillation strategy that gradually reduces teacher influence when it stops helping.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of turning sparse trajectory-level RL rewards into useful token-level supervision for multi-turn agents, while avoiding over-reliance on a self-teacher that may be inaccurate or only helpful during certain training phases.
method: Uses on-policy distillation to transfer dense token-level guidance from a self-teacher to a skill-free student.
Introduces a self-retiring mechanism that detects when teacher supervision becomes less reliable or less useful and reduces its influence over training.
Adapts the distillation process to the stage-dependent nature of agentic RL, where teacher help is strongest early or in specific phases and weaker later.
impact: RetireOPD can make agent training more stable and efficient by using teacher guidance only when it truly helps. This is useful for practitioners building multi-turn AI agents that must learn from sparse rewards without inheriting teacher mistakes.

paper_title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yan Yu, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, Yichen Pan, Aozhe Wang
